title: 90792 CPT Code: Psychiatric Evaluation Billing Rules for 2026
summary: The 90792 CPT code covers a psychiatric evaluation with medical services. Who can bill it, what it pays in 2026, and what you cannot bill on the same day.
body_markdown:
The 90792 CPT code is the psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services. It is the intake code for prescribers whose first visit includes medical work, such as prescribing or ordering labs. Psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners report it for that visit. Whether it pays turns on what the evaluation contains and what else you bill that day. It also turns on whether an office visit code would have fit better.


Every rule below is taken from a primary source and attributed where it appears. Where a rule belongs to one Medicare contractor or to the individual payer, this page says so. The sources are:


- The CMS[Medicare NCCI Policy Manual, Chapter XI](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/11-chapter11a-ncci-medicare-policy-manual-2026-final.pdf) , revised January 1, 2026
- First Coast Service Options LCD[L33252](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/lcd.aspx?lcdid=33252) and billing article[A57520](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/article.aspx?articleId=57520) , the Medicare contractor for Florida, Puerto Rico and the US Virgin Islands
- The CMS 2026[physician fee schedule relative value file](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-schedules/physician/pfs-relative-value-files) , January release
- The CMS[CY 2026 list of Medicare telehealth services](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/telehealth/list-services)
- The American Psychiatric Association[CPT Primer for Psychiatrists](https://www.psychiatry.org/File%20Library/Psychiatrists/Practice/Practice-Management/Coding-Reimbursement-Medicare-Medicaid/Coding-Reimbursement/cpt-primer-for-psychiatrists.pdf)

Timed No. The descriptor carries no time CMS 2026 fee schedule file

Same day as an office E/M visit E&M codes 99202 to 99215 are not reported with it NCCI Chapter XI, section C


Interactive complexity add-on 90785 can be reported with it First Coast A57520


Medicare telehealth, 2026 On the list, status Maintain CMS CY 2026 telehealth list


2026 national Medicare amount USD 202.08 office, USD 159.32 facility CMS 2026 RVUs x 33.4009


How often Once at the onset of an illness, repeatable in defined cases First Coast L33252


## What is CPT code 90792?


CPT code 90792 reports an initial psychiatric diagnostic evaluation that includes medical services. The APA primer describes it as an initial diagnostic interview for an adult or adolescent that includes medical services. It names the chief complaint, history of present illness, review of pertinent systems, family and psychosocial history, and a complete mental status examination. On top of that sits the medical work: ordering and interpreting labs or other studies, or prescribing medication.


The NCCI manual puts the split in one line. 90791 is psychiatric evaluation without medical E&M, and 90792 is psychiatric evaluation with medical E&M. The medical component is the whole reason the second code exists.


Element of the 90792 descriptor What it looks like in the note


Chief complaint Reason for the visit in the patient's words


History of present illness Onset, duration, course and severity of symptoms


Review of pertinent systems Sleep, appetite, energy, pain, other relevant systems


Family and psychosocial history Family psychiatric history, living situation, work, supports, substance use


Complete mental status examination Appearance, behavior, speech, mood, affect, thought process and content, cognition, insight, judgment


Medical services Medication started or changed, labs or studies ordered and interpreted, physical examination elements as indicated


## What does a 90792 evaluation have to include?


First Coast LCD[L33252](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/lcd.aspx?lcdid=33252) defines the evaluation with medical services as an integrated biopsychosocial and medical assessment. It lists history, psychiatric history, a complete mental status exam and other physical examination elements as indicated. It adds a tentative diagnosis and an evaluation of the patient's ability and willingness to take part in the proposed treatment plan. The same LCD lists what the record should contain:


1. The reason for the evaluation or the patient's chief complaint
2. A referral source, if applicable
3. History of present illness, including how long the problems have existed
4. Past psychiatric history
5. Significant medical history and current medications
6. Social history
7. Family history
8. Mental status exam
9. Strengths and liabilities
10. A diagnostic impression or problem list
11. A treatment plan


The record should also show a psychiatric illness, or emotional or behavioral symptoms that suggest one or significantly alter baseline functioning. That is the medical necessity line in L33252. L33252 is one contractor's policy. Other Medicare contractors and commercial payers publish their own, and most cover the same ground.


## Who can bill 90792?


First Coast billing article[A57520](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/article.aspx?articleId=57520) covers the evaluation with medical assessment. It says the physician or non-physician practitioner may use 90792 or an E/M code. The deciding factor is scope. The clinician has to be licensed to deliver the medical services the code describes.


Clinician Intake code that fits Why


Psychiatrist 90792 or a new patient E/M code Medical services are in scope


Psychiatric nurse practitioner (PMHNP) 90792 or a new patient E/M code A non-physician practitioner under A57520, within state scope


Physician assistant in psychiatry 90792 or a new patient E/M code A non-physician practitioner under A57520, within state scope


Psychologist, LCSW, LPC, LMFT 90791 The evaluation carries no medical services


- The license and the work done both have to support the medical component.
- A prescriber who does an evaluation with no medical work at all is describing 90791.
- Payer credentialing rules still apply. Check which codes each plan lets each license bill.


## 90792 vs 90791: which one applies?


The split is the medical services. If the evaluation includes prescribing, ordering or interpreting labs, or other medical work, it is 90792. If it does not, it is 90791. The content of the psychiatric interview is otherwise the same.


90791 90792


Descriptor Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services


Typical clinician Therapist or psychologist Psychiatrist or PMHNP


Medical services None Prescribing, labs, physical exam elements as indicated


2026 national RVUs, office 5.19 6.05


2026 national Medicare amount, office USD 173.35 USD 202.08


Same-day psychotherapy Not separately reportable Not separately reportable


For the therapist side of the intake, see our[90791 CPT code guide](https://www.mdhub.ai/blog-posts/90791-cpt-code) , which covers the two codes side by side in more detail.


## 90792 vs 99204 and 99205: which should a prescriber bill?


A prescriber seeing a new patient has two routes. One is 90792. The other is a new patient office visit, 99204 or 99205, picked by medical decision making or total time. First Coast A57520 allows either. The NCCI manual rules out billing both for the same evaluation. The choice changes what else you can bill that day.


90792 99204 99205


CMS short descriptor Psych diag eval w/med srvcs Office o/p new mod 45 min Office o/p new hi 60 min


How the level is set No levels and no time Moderate decision making or 45 minutes High decision making or 60 minutes


Psychotherapy add-on 90833, 90836 or 90838 No. Add-ons go with E&M Yes, if separately identifiable Yes, if separately identifiable


2026 national RVUs, office 6.05 5.31 7.09


2026 national Medicare amount, office USD 202.08 USD 177.36 USD 236.81


2026 national Medicare amount, facility USD 159.32 USD 116.90 USD 160.32


Read the table as a decision, in this order:


1. If you also deliver psychotherapy at the first visit and want to bill it, use the E/M route. NCCI lists 90833, 90836 and 90838 as add-ons to an E&M code, and 90792 cannot carry psychotherapy on the same date.
2. If decision making is high or total time reaches 60 minutes, 99205 carries more relative value than 90792 under Medicare.
3. If the visit supports 99204 and no more, 90792 carries more relative value than 99204 in the office setting.
4. If the payer requires 90792 for psychiatric intakes, follow the contract. Some plans set their own code rules.


Under the E/M route, keep the psychotherapy time separate. First Coast A57520 asks for the start and stop times or total time of the psychotherapy. That total does not include the E/M time.

## What does 90792 pay in 2026?


Medicare pays 90792 from the national[2026 relative value file](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/payment/fee-schedules/physician/pfs-relative-value-files) . The January release lists 90792 at 6.05 total RVUs in the office and 4.77 in a facility. The 2026 conversion factor in the same file is 33.4009. That gives a national amount of USD 202.08 in the office and USD 159.32 in a facility, before the geographic adjustment for your locality.


Code Descriptor (CMS short form) Office RVUs Office amount (USD) Facility RVUs Facility amount (USD)


90792 Psych diag eval w/med srvcs 6.05 202.08 4.77 159.32


90791 Psych diagnostic evaluation 5.19 173.35 4.11 137.28


90785 Psytx complex interactive 0.44 14.70 0.35 11.69


99204 Office o/p new mod 45 min 5.31 177.36 3.50 116.90


99205 Office o/p new hi 60 min 7.09 236.81 4.80 160.32


90833 Psytx w pt w e/m 30 min 2.44 81.50 1.97 65.80


90836 Psytx w pt w e/m 45 min 3.09 103.21 2.49 83.17


90838 Psytx w pt w e/m 60 min 4.09 136.61 3.30 110.22


- These are national Medicare figures from total RVUs times the conversion factor. Your locality adjusts them.
- The CMS[physician fee schedule look-up](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/physician-fee-schedule/search) shows the amount for your locality.
- The file carries a second, higher conversion factor for qualifying alternative payment model participants. This page uses the standard one.
- Commercial plans and Medicaid set their own rates. Your contract is the number that counts.
- Facility amounts apply where the facility bills its own costs, such as a hospital outpatient department.


## Can you bill 90792 and 90833 together?


No. The[NCCI manual](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/11-chapter11a-ncci-medicare-policy-manual-2026-final.pdf) gives the reason. Psychotherapy includes continuing psychiatric evaluation, so 90791 and 90792 are not separately reportable with any psychotherapy code on the same date. It also lists 90833, 90836 and 90838 as add-ons reported with the appropriate E&M code, and 90792 is not an E&M code.


Say the first visit includes a medical evaluation and psychotherapy you want to bill. The NCCI-consistent route is a new patient E/M code plus the psychotherapy add-on. The two services need to be separately identifiable in the note, with the psychotherapy time recorded on its own.


## What can you not bill with 90792 on the same day?


Code or group Same date as 90792 Source


Individual psychotherapy 90832, 90834, 90837 Not separately reportable NCCI Chapter XI, section C


Psychotherapy add-ons 90833, 90836, 90838 Not reportable. They attach to E&M NCCI Chapter XI, section C


Group and family psychotherapy 90853, 90846, 90847 Not separately reportable NCCI Chapter XI, section C


Psychotherapy for crisis 90839, 90840 Not reported with 90791 or 90792 NCCI Chapter XI and First Coast A57520


Office E&M 99202 to 99215 Not reported with either diagnostic code NCCI Chapter XI, section C


Neurobehavioral status exam 96116, 96121 Not reported with 90791 or 90792 NCCI Chapter XI, section M


Psychological testing and evaluation 96130 to 96146 Only as distinct services, with no duplicated time NCCI Chapter XI, section M


Interactive complexity 90785 Reportable when documented First Coast A57520


## Can you bill 90785 with 90792?


Yes. First Coast[A57520](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/article.aspx?articleId=57520) lists the diagnostic evaluation codes 90791 and 90792 among the codes interactive complexity is used with. The NCCI manual describes interactive services as being for patients who lack the expressive language to explain their symptoms and response to treatment.


- Document what made the encounter interactive, such as a caregiver whose involvement complicated the visit.
- A57520 says 90785 should not be billed when a patient is unable to communicate by any means.
- The main example in the APA primer is the treatment of children.
- The 2026 national Medicare amount for 90785 is USD 14.70 in the office.


## How often can you bill 90792?


First Coast LCD[L33252](https://www.cms.gov/medicare-coverage-database/view/lcd.aspx?lcdid=33252) says a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation can be conducted once, at the onset of an illness or suspected illness. It says routine repeat evaluations of patients with chronic conditions are not medically necessary. The same provider may repeat it in these cases:


Repeat allowed by L33252 when What to document


An extended hiatus in treatment The date last seen. L33252 defines the hiatus as generally 6 months since the last visit


Admission to inpatient care for a psychiatric illness The admission and the reason


A significant change in mental status What changed and why reassessment is needed


Established neurological disorder or dementia with an acute change The acute or marked mental status change


A second opinion or diagnostic clarification The question being answered


The APA primer adds that the code can be billed on subsequent days when an extended evaluation is medically necessary. Its example is a child who has to be seen with and without the parents. Commercial plans can set their own frequency limits, so check the plan before a repeat evaluation.


## Is 90792 covered for telehealth in 2026?


Yes, for Medicare. The CMS[CY 2026 final list of Medicare telehealth services](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/telehealth/list-services) carries 90792 with the status Maintain. 90791, 90785 and the psychotherapy add-ons 90833, 90836 and 90838 are on the list too.


- The list tells you the code is payable via telehealth under Medicare. It does not set modifiers or place of service.
- Modifier and place of service rules come from the payer and change by year.
- Commercial and Medicaid coverage of telehealth is set plan by plan and by state law.


## What do payers check on a 90792 note?


A reviewer reads the note against the descriptor and the payer's policy. Build the evaluation so each check can be answered from the page.


Check Passes when the note shows Fails when


Medical services present A medication decision, labs ordered or interpreted, or exam elements The visit reads as a therapy intake only


Complete mental status exam Every domain, including cognition, insight and judgment Mood and affect are the only entries


Medical necessity Symptoms that suggest a psychiatric illness or alter functioning Symptoms are absent or generic


Diagnosis A tentative diagnosis or impression list coded to the highest specificity The diagnosis field is empty or unspecified


Treatment plan A plan and the patient's ability and willingness to take part No plan or next step


Same-day services No psychotherapy or E&M billed on the same date 90833 or 99204 sits on the same claim


Repeat evaluation The hiatus, admission or change in status that justifies it A second 90792 with no reason given


Interactive complexity What made the encounter interactive 90785 billed with no explanation


## Why do 90792 claims get denied, and how do you fix them?


Denial cause Rule behind it Fix


Psychotherapy billed on the same date NCCI Chapter XI, section C Bill a new patient E/M plus the add-on, or drop the psychotherapy line


Office E/M billed with 90792 NCCI Chapter XI, section C Pick one route for the evaluation


Crisis codes billed with 90792 NCCI Chapter XI and First Coast A57520 Bill the crisis service on its own


Repeat evaluation without a qualifying reason First Coast L33252 Document the hiatus, admission or change in status, or bill an E/M follow-up


No medical services in the note The 90792 descriptor Code 90791, or document the medical work done


Clinician without medical scope billed it First Coast A57520 and payer credentialing Code 90791 under that clinician


Diagnosis does not support medical necessity The covered ICD-10-CM list in A57520 Code the diagnosis to the highest specificity


90785 with no documented reason First Coast A57520 Document what made the visit interactive, or drop the add-on

## What should a 90792 note look like?


This outline covers the L33252 record list and the descriptor, plus substance use history and a risk assessment:


1. Identifying information and referral source
2. Reason for the evaluation and chief complaint
3. History of present illness, with onset and duration
4. Past psychiatric history, including prior treatment and hospitalizations
5. Medical history and current medications
6. Substance use history
7. Family psychiatric history
8. Social history
9. Review of pertinent systems
10. Mental status examination, every domain
11. Risk assessment
12. Strengths and liabilities
13. Diagnostic impression or problem list
14. Medical services delivered: medication decision, labs or studies ordered, exam findings
15. Treatment plan and the patient's ability and willingness to take part


Run these checks before the claim goes out:


- The note shows at least one medical service.
- The mental status exam covers every domain.
- No psychotherapy code is on the same date of service.
- No office E/M code is on the same date of service.
- Any repeat evaluation states the hiatus, admission or change in status.
- 90785, if billed, names what made the visit interactive.
- The clinician's license and payer credentialing allow 90792.
- The diagnosis is coded to the highest specificity.
- For telehealth, the payer's modifier and place of service rules are applied.


## A 90792 example: choosing the code for a new patient


This scenario is illustrative and the patient is invented. A PMHNP sees a new adult patient for low mood and poor sleep. She takes a full history, completes a mental status exam, orders a thyroid panel, and starts an antidepressant. She spends some of the visit on supportive therapy but does not plan to bill it.


Question Answer for this visit Code effect


Were medical services delivered? Yes. Labs ordered and a medication started 90792 or E/M


Is psychotherapy being billed? No 90792 remains open


Decision making level Moderate 99204 would apply under the E/M route


Which route carries more under Medicare, office setting? 90792 at 6.05 RVUs vs 99204 at 5.31 90792


Same-day services on the claim None Clean


Change one fact and the answer moves. If she had delivered 20 minutes of separately identifiable psychotherapy and wanted to bill it, the claim becomes 99204 plus 90833. If decision making had been high, 99205 would carry more than 90792.

## 90792 CPT code FAQ


### What is the difference between CPT 90791 and 90792?


90792 includes medical services such as prescribing or ordering and interpreting labs. 90791 does not. The NCCI manual describes 90791 as psychiatric evaluation without medical E&M and 90792 as psychiatric evaluation with medical E&M.


### Is 90792 a timed code?


No. The descriptor carries no time, so the code is not selected by minutes.


### How many times a year can you bill 90792?


First Coast LCD L33252 allows it once at the onset of an illness. Repeats are allowed after a hiatus of generally 6 months, an inpatient admission, or a significant change in mental status. Commercial plans set their own limits.


### What pays more, 90792 or 99205?


Under the 2026 national Medicare fee schedule, 99205 carries 7.09 office RVUs and 90792 carries 6.05. 99205 needs high decision making or 60 minutes of total time to support it. Commercial rates depend on the contract.


### Does 90792 pay more than 99204?


Under the 2026 national Medicare fee schedule, 90792 carries 6.05 office RVUs and 99204 carries 5.31. In a facility the figures are 4.77 and 3.50.


### Can you bill 90792 and 90833 together?


No. The NCCI manual says 90792 is not separately reportable with psychotherapy on the same date, and 90833 is an add-on to an E&M code. Bill a new patient E/M plus 90833 instead.


### Can you bill 90792 with an E/M code on the same day?


No. The NCCI manual says E&M codes 99202 to 99215 shall not be reported with 90791 or 90792.


### Can a nurse practitioner bill 90792?


Yes, within state scope. First Coast A57520 says the physician or non-physician practitioner may use 90792 or an E/M code for an evaluation with medical assessment.


### Can a psychologist or therapist bill 90792?


Generally no. A clinician whose evaluation includes no medical services reports 90791.


### Is 90792 covered by Medicare for telehealth in 2026?


Yes. The CMS CY 2026 final list of Medicare telehealth services carries 90792 with the status Maintain.


### Can 90785 be added to 90792?


Yes, when interactive complexity is documented. First Coast A57520 lists 90792 among the codes 90785 is used with.


### What is the difference between 90792 and 99215?


90792 is an initial psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services. 99215 is an office visit for an established patient at a high level, used for ongoing medication management once the evaluation is done.
